metadata.title: Is the Third Judge Necessary?
metadata.audience: Students and practitioners learning to use and report on AI systems
metadata.fellow: Janvi Chitroda, AI Data Engineer volunteer, Medhavy project, Humanitarians AI
metadata.source: inbox/term2-week07/term2-week7-video-content.md (Week 7); narration supplied verbatim and pre-approved by Janvi (2026-10-27)
metadata.note: Project update. Thesis: before removing a part of a system, measure what changes without it — the third judge (GPT-4o-mini) is the tiebreaker, not redundant; a planted-error test with two judges caught 30.0% strictly and needs a three-judge rerun. Experiments and scripts are Janvi's. Only Professor Brown may be named. Every on-screen number appears in the Week 7 source as written.

beats.role_note: COLD OPEN LAW — Claude composer, ask lands answered. Required intro line + AI-narration disclosure.
beats.narration_text: Hi, I am Janvi and this video is about two experiments: whether our third judge is necessary, and how often the ensemble catches planted errors. This narration is an AI-generated voice; the work is mine.

props.command: Could we drop one of our three AI judges? What should I measure before removing it?
output: Rerun the vote without that judge
Count what changes: review queue, shipped items
Test detection on errors you planted

beats.role_note: Three judge logos (ink); GPT-4o-mini dimmed with chip 'most frequent dissenter'; question 'drop it?'; Mistral + Claude kept.
beats.narration_text: Our kappa results showed G P T four o mini was the most frequent dissenter. So the obvious question: could we drop it, and keep just Mistral and Claude?
beats.visual_intent: Three judge logos (ink); GPT-4o-mini dimmed with chip 'most frequent dissenter'; question 'drop it?'; Mistral + Claude kept.

beats.role_note: Ablation card '10,048 valid rows'; 'Mistral + Claude agree 73.8%'; review queue bars 585 → 2,631, '4.5-fold'.
beats.narration_text: I built an ablation test on 10,048 valid keyword rows. Mistral and Claude agree on 73.8 percent of items. With only two judges, every disagreement goes to a human, so the review queue grows from 585 items to 2,631, about four and a half times larger.
beats.visual_intent: Ablation card '10,048 valid rows'; 'Mistral + Claude agree 73.8%'; review queue bars 585 → 2,631, '4.5-fold'.

beats.role_note: Chips: '2,046 items change action (20.4%)' · 'tie broken by GPT-4o-mini' · '33% API cost saved' · '1,799 fewer shipped'.
beats.narration_text: And 2,046 items, 20.4 percent, change outcome. In every one, G P T four o mini had broken the tie. Dropping it would save about a third of the API cost, but ship 1,799 fewer items.
beats.visual_intent: Chips: '2,046 items change action (20.4%)' · 'tie broken by GPT-4o-mini' · '33% API cost saved' · '1,799 fewer shipped'.

beats.role_note: Verdict card 'not redundant: the tiebreaker' with the GPT-4o-mini mark.
beats.narration_text: So the third judge isn't redundant. It's the tiebreaker.
beats.visual_intent: Verdict card 'not redundant: the tiebreaker' with the GPT-4o-mini mark.

beats.role_note: 200 approved definitions → 150 corrupted (5 types × 30) + 50 controls; type chips: conflation · wrong expansion · disambiguation · factual error · category swap.
beats.narration_text: The second experiment asked a harder question: does the ensemble catch wrong definitions? Instead of trusting my own judgment, I built ground truth by corrupting 150 good definitions in five ways, like swapping a gene's role or using the wrong abbreviation expansion, and kept 50 untouched as controls.
beats.visual_intent: 200 approved definitions → 150 corrupted (5 types × 30) + 50 controls; type chips: conflation · wrong expansion · disambiguation · factual error · category swap.

show.event: does the ensemble catch wrong definitions?

beats.role_note: Chip 'Claude not in this run'; stacked bar of the 150 corrupted: caught 30.0% · sent to review 51.3% · passed through 18.7%; controls flagged 0.0%.
beats.narration_text: Claude wasn't available for this run, so two judges scored them blind. They strictly caught 30 percent, sent 51.3 percent to review, and let 18.7 percent through. No control was flagged.
beats.visual_intent: Chip 'Claude not in this run'; stacked bar of the 150 corrupted: caught 30.0% · sent to review 51.3% · passed through 18.7%; controls flagged 0.0%.

beats.role_note: Card 'next: rerun with all three' with three ink logos. (Split from Janvi's B07 so the handoff stays a pure composer beat; narration verbatim.)
beats.narration_text: Two judges weren't enough to trust that result, so the next step is a rerun with all three.
beats.visual_intent: Card 'next: rerun with all three' with three ink logos. (Split from Janvi's B07 so the handoff stays a pure composer beat; narration verbatim.)
